requirements.quote:
The answer, authority, and additional sections all share the same
format: a variable number of resource records, where the number of
records is specified in the corresponding count field in the header.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the answer, authority, or additional section of a message.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent each section as a variable number of resource records.
requirements.why_checkable: Section serialization and parsing can be checked for a resource-record sequence.

requirements.quote:
The answer, authority, and additional sections all share the same
format: a variable number of resource records, where the number of
records is specified in the corresponding count field in the header.
requirements.condition: For each answer, authority, or additional section of a message.
requirements.required_behavior: Make the number of resource records in the section equal to the corresponding count field in the header.
requirements.why_checkable: Count the encoded records in each section and compare with its header count.

requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the field order NAME, TYPE, CLASS, TTL, RDLENGTH, RDATA.
requirements.why_checkable: Record field offsets and serialization order can be inspected and exercised.

requirements.quote: NAME            a domain name to which this resource record pertains.
requirements.condition: For the NAME field of a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the domain name to which the resource record pertains.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded NAME can be decoded and compared with the record owner domain name.

requirements.quote:
TYPE            two octets containing one of the RR type codes.  This
                field specifies the meaning of the data in the RDATA
                field.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the TYPE field of a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Use exactly two octets for TYPE.
requirements.why_checkable: TYPE field width can be checked in wire encodings and parser offsets.

requirements.quote:
TYPE            two octets containing one of the RR type codes.  This
                field specifies the meaning of the data in the RDATA
                field.
requirements.condition: For the TYPE field of a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Use an RR type code to identify the meaning of the data in RDATA.
requirements.why_checkable: The type-code mapping and interpretation of RDATA can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
CLASS           two octets which specify the class of the data in the
                RDATA field.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the CLASS field of a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Use exactly two octets for CLASS.
requirements.why_checkable: CLASS field width can be checked in wire encodings and parser offsets.

requirements.quote:
CLASS           two octets which specify the class of the data in the
                RDATA field.
requirements.condition: For the CLASS field of a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Use CLASS to specify the class of the data in RDATA.
requirements.why_checkable: Record-class metadata can be compared with the encoded CLASS and RDATA interpretation.

requirements.quote:
TTL             a 32 bit unsigned integer that specifies the time
                interval (in seconds) that the resource record may be
                cached before it should be discarded.  Zero values are
                interpreted to mean that the RR can only be used for the
                transaction in progress, and should not be cached.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the TTL field of a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent TTL as a 32-bit unsigned integer.
requirements.why_checkable: TTL width and unsigned range can be checked using wire values, including values with the high bit set.

requirements.quote:
TTL             a 32 bit unsigned integer that specifies the time
                interval (in seconds) that the resource record may be
                cached before it should be discarded.  Zero values are
                interpreted to mean that the RR can only be used for the
                transaction in progress, and should not be cached.
requirements.condition: When interpreting the TTL of a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret TTL as a time interval measured in seconds.
requirements.why_checkable: Cache lifetime calculations can be checked against the integer TTL and elapsed seconds.

requirements.quote:
TTL             a 32 bit unsigned integer that specifies the time
                interval (in seconds) that the resource record may be
                cached before it should be discarded.  Zero values are
                interpreted to mean that the RR can only be used for the
                transaction in progress, and should not be cached.
requirements.condition: When a resource record is cached and the interval specified by its TTL has elapsed.
requirements.required_behavior: The cached resource record should be discarded.
requirements.why_checkable: Cache-expiration behavior can be observed after advancing time beyond the TTL; the source states this as should behavior.

requirements.quote:
TTL             a 32 bit unsigned integer that specifies the time
                interval (in seconds) that the resource record may be
                cached before it should be discarded.  Zero values are
                interpreted to mean that the RR can only be used for the
                transaction in progress, and should not be cached.
requirements.condition: When a resource record has a TTL of zero.
requirements.required_behavior: Limit use of the resource record to the transaction in progress.
requirements.why_checkable: A zero-TTL record can be exercised across transaction boundaries to check its permitted scope.

requirements.quote:
TTL             a 32 bit unsigned integer that specifies the time
                interval (in seconds) that the resource record may be
                cached before it should be discarded.  Zero values are
                interpreted to mean that the RR can only be used for the
                transaction in progress, and should not be cached.
requirements.condition: When a resource record has a TTL of zero.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The resource record should not be cached.
requirements.why_checkable: Cache insertion or retention of zero-TTL records can be inspected; the source expresses a should-not recommendation.

requirements.quote:
RDLENGTH        an unsigned 16 bit integer that specifies the length in
                octets of the RDATA field.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the RDLENGTH field of a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent RDLENGTH as an unsigned 16-bit integer.
requirements.why_checkable: Field width and unsigned bounds can be verified in serialization and parsing.

requirements.quote:
RDLENGTH        an unsigned 16 bit integer that specifies the length in
                octets of the RDATA field.
requirements.condition: For the RDLENGTH field of a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or interpret RDLENGTH as the number of octets in the RDATA field.
requirements.why_checkable: Compare RDLENGTH against the actual encoded RDATA byte count.

requirements.quote:
RDATA           a variable length string of octets that describes the
                resource.  The format of this information varies
                according to the TYPE and CLASS of the resource record.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the RDATA field of a resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent RDATA as a variable-length string of octets describing the resource.
requirements.why_checkable: The RDATA representation and handling of varying byte lengths can be checked.

requirements.quote:
RDATA           a variable length string of octets that describes the
                resource.  The format of this information varies
                according to the TYPE and CLASS of the resource record.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the RDATA format associated with both the TYPE and CLASS of the resource record.
requirements.why_checkable: RDATA codec dispatch can be inspected for dependence on both type and class.

requirements.quote:
RDATA           a variable length string of octets that describes the
                resource.  The format of this information varies
                according to the TYPE and CLASS of the resource record.
                For example, the if the TYPE is A and the CLASS is IN,
                the RDATA field is a 4 octet ARPA Internet address.
requirements.condition: When a resource record has TYPE A and CLASS IN.
requirements.required_behavior: Use an RDATA field exactly four octets long.
requirements.why_checkable: An A record in class IN has a directly checkable RDATA byte count.

requirements.quote:
RDATA           a variable length string of octets that describes the
                resource.  The format of this information varies
                according to the TYPE and CLASS of the resource record.
                For example, the if the TYPE is A and the CLASS is IN,
                the RDATA field is a 4 octet ARPA Internet address.
requirements.condition: When a resource record has TYPE A and CLASS IN.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret RDATA as an ARPA Internet address.
requirements.why_checkable: The A/IN RDATA codec can be checked for Internet-address representation.
